Order 
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is an accused in Crime No. 332/2024 of Mararikulam Police Station, Alappuzha,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short, 'IPC') and Sections 66, 66(C) and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act,
2000 (for short, 'IT Act').
3.

According to the prosecution, the accused had, during the period 29.03.2024 to 30.03.2024,
cheated the defacto complainant and obtained a large amount of money and transferred Rs.1,25,340/- to different google pay accounts under the promise of providing an employment and thereafter failed to provide the job or return the amount and thereby committed the offences alleged.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner has been falsely arrayed as an accused and that he has no involvement in the alleged crime.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.

7. Though petitioner was not initially arrayed as an accused, the investigation conducted so far revealed that bank accounts were opened by other persons at the instance of the petitioner, and he had even paid commission to those persons for opening such accounts.
It was also pointed out that the petitioner is involved in another crime of a similar nature.
8. Having regard to the above circumstances, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to protect the petitioner with an order of pre-arrest bail.
Accordingly, this bail application is dismissed.

However, if the petitioner surrenders before the Investigating Officer on 19.08.2025, he shall be subjected to interrogation, and thereafter, if the petitioner is arrested, he shall be produced before the jurisdictional court without undue delay.
If any application for bail is filed, the same shall also be considered in accordance with law.
